notes: Checked at this exact model, but from a distributor spec table and Dell's own marketing copy quoted in retailer listings - Dell's product page could not be opened from the session this was researched in, so nothing here comes from dell.com directly. 120 Hz applies to DisplayPort and Thunderbolt 4; HDMI is 100 Hz. The five-star TUV Rheinland Eye Comfort rating is the one claim worth re-checking yourself, because it is the reason this model ranks first: Dell's copy states it was the first 34-inch monitor to earn five stars, and the five-star tier requires at least 120 Hz, which this panel has and the 60 Hz UltraSharp 34s do not. Contrast 2000:1 is the IPS Black figure and is a claim, not a measurement. No DisplayHDR tier was found in any listing, so the HDR field is left empty rather than guessed. VRR is not stated anywhere I saw; left unknown rather than assumed absent.

Checked at this exact model against Asus's own technical specification page. 120 Hz over DisplayPort and USB-C, 100 Hz over HDMI; FreeSync Premium Pro to 120 Hz. Stand does height, tilt and swivel over 0-115 mm but does not pivot. Curvature is deliberately left empty: no source consulted stated a radius, and this range includes both flat and curved models, so guessing would be worse than the scoring's neutral unknown band. KVM is left unknown for the same reason - the spec page sections I saw did not mention one either way. Launch year not established.

Checked at this exact model across a review and two spec tables. Refresh is recorded as 144 Hz native rather than the 160 Hz some spec tables print, because the sources that distinguish the two call 160 Hz an overclock; recording the overclock as native would flatter it against panels that do 144 Hz without one. The quoted 1 ms is given as MPRT by one source and GtG by another, which is exactly the claim the scoring refuses to award a top band to. USB-C and KVM are set to absent rather than unknown on the strength of a full port list (DP 1.4, 2x HDMI 2.0, 2x USB 3.0, audio) that contains neither. Curvature radius not stated by any source seen.

Carried from the 34GP83A, not checked independently. The review cited states the 34GN850 has identical specifications to the 34GP83A and differs only in the rear logo and the OSD layout, while often costing more. It is on the list because it is the same panel at a different price, which is precisely what the cross-shop rule is for; every figure here is the sibling's. If a shop ever shows it cheaper than the 34GP83A, that is a real find rather than a matching error.

Checked at this exact model against a review and retailer tables. Flat, not curved - it is the successor to a curved VA model, which is worth knowing if the curve matters to you. KVM is confirmed by the review, which describes switching one keyboard and mouse set between computers. USB-C power delivery is 15 W, which three independent sources agree on (TechPowerUp's spec table and review, MonitorNerds, and a Polish review); one retailer listing says 18 W and two others say the port has no power delivery at all. MonitorNerds puts it plainly: at 15 W a USB-C laptop still needs its own adapter. Whichever of those figures is right, none of them charges a laptop, which is what the 65 W floor exists to catch. The 1 ms figure is MPRT. No DisplayHDR certification was found, only 'HDR' in marketing copy, so the HDR field is empty.
